phrases.translation: Glorify the Name of your Lord, the Most High
phrases.text: Glorify the name of your Lord and declare it free, that is, free of your calling by that name anything other than God. Some said it means glorify your Lord, the Most High, and the Prophet and his companions used to say, glory be to my Lord, the Most High, when they recited it.

phrases.translation: Who created and ˹perfectly˺ fashioned ˹all˺
phrases.text: He is the One who created all things and made them perfectly, and made them balanced.

phrases.translation: and Who ordained precisely and inspired accordingly
phrases.text: And He who determined the measure of things and then guided them. The commentators differed: some said He guided people to the way of good and evil and the cattle to their pastures, others that He guided the males to the females. Tabari keeps the guidance general, and notes that the reciters all agree the word is doubled.

phrases.translation: and Who brings forth ˹green˺ pasture
phrases.text: And He who brought forth the pasture from the earth for the livestock, the various kinds of crops and herbs, which spring up in colours you can see: yellow, red and white.

phrases.translation: then reduces it to withered chaff
phrases.text: And He made that grass into dry debris, withered and brown after the drought, so that the wind carries it away. The commentators say it becomes dry after it has been green, and that the torrents and the winds sweep it off.

phrases.translation: We will have you recite ˹the Quran, O Prophet,˺ so you will not forget ˹any of it˺
phrases.text: We will make you recite this Qur'an, O Muhammad, and you will not forget it. This is both a promise that God is teaching you and keeping it safe with you, and a command to you not to rush to recite it, as He says: do not move your tongue with it to hasten with it.

phrases.translation: unless Allah wills otherwise.
phrases.text: Except what God wills, meaning that we will make you forget it by abrogating it and removing it from the recitation.

phrases.translation: He surely knows what is open and what is hidden
phrases.text: He knows what you show openly and what you keep hidden, so be on your guard, in any state, against doing anything He has not permitted you.

phrases.translation: We will facilitate for you the Way of Ease
phrases.text: We will make it easy for you, O Muhammad, to do the good, which is the easiest of things.

phrases.translation: So ˹always˺ remind ˹with the Quran˺—˹even˺ if the reminder is beneficial ˹only to some˺
phrases.text: So remind, O Muhammad, the servants of God of His greatness, and warn them of His punishment. If the reminder benefits, meaning those about whom He has made you despair of their faith, for it does not benefit them.

phrases.translation: Those in awe ˹of Allah˺ will be mindful ˹of it˺
phrases.text: He who fears God and dreads His punishment will take heed of the reminder.

phrases.translation: But it will be shunned by the most wretched
phrases.text: The most wretched of the two groups avoids it, and they are the ones for whom the reminder was of no use. Qatada adds: no servant turns away from this reminder out of hatred for it, except a wretched one whose wretchedness is plain.

phrases.translation: who will burn in the greatest Fire
phrases.text: He who will enter the fire of Hell, and that is the greatest Fire, meaning the intensity of its heat and its pain.

phrases.translation: where they will not ˹be able to˺ live or die
phrases.text: Thereafter he does not die in the Fire, nor does he live. His soul comes to rest in his throat and does not go out, so that he does not die, nor return to its place, so that he does not live.
phrases.ar: ثُمَّ لَا يَمُوتُ فِيهَا وَلَا يَحۡيَىٰ

phrases.translation: Successful indeed are those who purify themselves
phrases.text: He has truly succeeded who purifies himself of disbelief and of disobedience, and acts on what God has commanded him. The commentators differed: some say it means he gives the alms of his wealth, others that he gives the alms of the breaking of the fast, and others that it means he professes that there is no god but God.

phrases.translation: remember the Name of their Lord, and pray
phrases.text: He remembered God, professed Him as one, called upon Him and longed for Him. And he prayed, meaning the prayers in which he remembered God with praise, glorification and supplication.

phrases.translation: But you ˹deniers only˺ prefer the life of this world
phrases.text: But you, O people, prefer the splendour of this world over the hereafter, and the people chose what perishes, except those God protected.

phrases.translation: even though the Hereafter is far better and more lasting
phrases.text: The hereafter is better for you and more lasting, because this world perishes while that does not. Ibn Masud said to his companions: we preferred this world because we saw its adornment, its food and its drink, while the hereafter was hidden from us.

phrases.translation: This is certainly ˹mentioned˺ in the earlier Scriptures—
phrases.text: The commentators differed about what this refers to: some said the verses of this surah, others the story of this surah, others this verse, that the hereafter is better and more lasting. Tabari holds that the earlier scriptures carried the same message.

phrases.translation: the Scriptures of Abraham and Moses
phrases.text: The scriptures of Abraham and Moses. Tabari says these words are in the earlier scriptures, and the books of God followed one another with this same message.
